markets.rules_primary: If the number of U.S. House seats won by candidates unaffiliated with a political party is at least 1 in the 2026 U.S. House elections, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A seat counts only if the relevant election authority records no political party designation for the winning candidate’s candidacy in the November 3, 2026 general election: Independent, Nonpartisan, No Party Preference, No Party Affiliation, Unaffiliated, Unenrolled, Undeclared, nomination by petition without a party designation, a declared write-in candidacy so recorded, or an equivalent. A candidate identified with a political party does not count, including a party whose registered name contains “Independent” such as the Independent Party of Oregon, and a candidate appearing on one ballot line without a designation and another with one. Caucus affiliation, endorsements and later party changes do not affect the count.

Only the regular general election in each of the 435 congressional districts for the term beginning January 3, 2027 counts; a special election for a 119th Congress vacancy is disregarded whenever held. No district counts twice.

Seats are counted from Designated Media Source calls as they stand at the Expiration time, not from House composition on any later date; the eight rank equally. A seat is counted when at least four have declared its winner with no contradictory declaration then outstanding; withdrawn or superseded declarations are disregarded. A seat not counted under that four-of-eight test is attributed to the candidate the state certifies as elected. A runoff seat is counted when that contest is called.

Designated Media Source declarations. For United States based elections, this Contract may be resolved on an accelerated basis if (A) at least four (4) of the eight (8) Designated Media Sources have declared a winning candidate, party, or option, and (B) none of the Designated Media Sources have issued a contradictory declaration. “Designated Media Sources” are: The New York Times (NYT), The Associated Press (AP), Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ), CNN, Fox News, NBC News, CBS News, and ABC News. Should one of the Designated Media Sources cease to provide independent election calls, it may be replaced at the sole discretion of the Exchange. For the purposes of this clause, a source declares a winning candidate, party, or option when it makes either (i) a formal projection of victory by its centralized decision desk, or (ii) an unambiguous statement in a news article that the candidate/party/option has won. For the network sources (Fox, NBC, CBS, ABC), a declaration from a local affiliate may represent the parent network; however, a declaration from the national desk shall always supersede any affiliate’s call. In all instances, a parent network and all of its affiliates shall collectively constitute a single source for the purpose of this clause.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early once the results deciding all 435 U.S. House seats in the 50 states have been certified.
markets.rules_primary: If the total vote count for all participants in the 2026 U.S. House elections in the 50 states is at least 119,000,000, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The count is the sum, across the 435 voting seats in the 2026 U.S. House elections in the 50 states (held Nov 3, 2026), of the formal votes each state's certifying authority certified for every candidate in the contest that decides each seat, including certified write-in votes. For a seat decided in a runoff after Nov 3, 2026 (such as Louisiana's Dec 12 runoffs), only the runoff's certified totals count, not that seat's Nov 3 totals. If a runoff is not held, that seat's Nov 3 totals count. In Maine and Alaska ranked-choice contests, the first-round (first-choice) totals are used. Unopposed candidates not printed on the ballot count as zero votes.

Each seat's certified result as of the moment the results deciding the last of these 435 seats are certified is used, including any recount certified by then. Later recounts, amendments or court changes do NOT count.

The following do NOT count:
Blank, void, over-, under- and exhausted ballots.
Delegate and Resident Commissioner elections (District of Columbia and the territories).
Special elections for the rest of a term ending Jan 3, 2027.

Running only for a lower post, such as Majority Leader or whip, does not count. For a person who announced before Issuance, repeating that announcement does not count; only standing as a candidate in a party's Speaker-nominee vote or accepting a floor nomination after Issuance counts. markets.rules_secondary:
Creating an AI select committee counts, whether in the House rules resolution for the 120th Congress or in a separate resolution. A committee under a different name, or one that also covers other technology subjects, counts if artificial intelligence is expressly named in its jurisdiction.

The following do NOT count:
An announcement or plan to establish the committee before the House adopts the resolution
A task force, commission, working group, caucus or subcommittee, including the House Democratic Commission on AI and the Innovation Economy
A select committee on another subject, such as China, whose jurisdiction mentions artificial intelligence only within that subject

Only reporting from the United States House of Representatives or any other Source Agency qualifies for the purposes of this market. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

markets.rules_primary: If the number of Arizona State Senate seats held by Republicans is at least 20 after the November 3, 2026 general election, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Each market counts the seats in that chamber held by the Republican Party when the chamber's November 3, 2026 general election results are certified. Every seat on the 2026 ballot is attributed to its certified winner, and every other seat to the party designation the state election authority recorded for the winner of that seat's most recent general or special election, regardless of any vacancy, appointment or party change since that election. The number shown is that state's constitutional requirement to override a governor's veto, applied to the chamber's full membership, including where the state measures it against members present and voting. Vacancies, appointments and party changes after certification, and special elections held after November 3, 2026, are disregarded.

A winner counts as Republican if the official results show the winner on the Republican Party's ballot line or, where they show a combined designation, list Republican first; a winner elected only on another party's line does not count.

markets.rules_primary: If the Federal Trade Commission announces opening an investigation into the acquisition, scanning and destruction of books by artificial intelligence companies for use in training AI models before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Only a public act of the Federal Trade Commission counts: a press release, a docketed Section 6(b) study order, a filed administrative or federal complaint, or an on-the-record statement by the Chair or a Commissioner confirming an investigation.

A statement by the Chair or a Commissioner in congressional testimony counts if it confirms an investigation into this practice
A statement of general concern, a request for public comment, or an acknowledgement of receiving the letter without confirming an investigation does NOT count
If the Commission opens an investigation but does not disclose it publicly before expiration, this market resolves NO
The investigation must concern the acquisition, scanning or destruction of books for training AI models. An unrelated artificial intelligence inquiry does NOT count

markets.rules_primary: If the Democratic party has below 53 Senate seats on Feb 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Clarification (11/12/26): Kalshi has filed an amendment to this market's Contract so that it can settle before February 1, 2027 once the election results have decided it. Starting November 26, 2026, Kalshi will check each party's seat count every day at 10:00 AM ET using Associated Press race calls, with a buffer for changes after the election (5 seats off the floor in the House, 1 in the Senate, and 1 seat added to the ceiling). Any market the results have decided will settle that morning; the rest will settle on February 1, 2027 as they do now. If the composition of Congress on February 1, 2027 would have paid an early-settled market the other way, Kalshi will credit $1.00 per contract for positions held on that side at 7:00 AM ET on November 12, 2026. Contracts bought after that time are not covered.

For example, as of November 11, 2026, the Associated Press has declared Democrats the winner of 254 House seats, with 13 seats undeclared. That gives Democrats a floor of 254 (seats declared) and a ceiling of 267 (254 plus the 13 undeclared), or 249 and 268 after the buffers. In KXDHOUSESEATS-27, every range from "Below 210" through "242-245" lies entirely below both values, so those markets would expire and settle No; "246-249" and "Above 249" each contain one of the two values, so they continue to trade and are checked again the next morning.

events.title: How many Senate seats will Democrats hold after the Midterms?

markets.rules_primary: If the number of U.S. House seats won by Democratic Party candidates is at least 210 in the 2026 U.S. House elections, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A seat counts only if the relevant election authority records a Democratic designation for the winning candidate’s candidacy in the November 3, 2026 general election; a recognized state affiliate (including the Minnesota Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party and the North Dakota Democratic-Nonpartisan League Party), any one of several ballot lines, or a declared write-in candidacy so recorded all qualify. Caucus affiliation, endorsements and later party changes do not affect the count: a member elected without a Democratic designation who caucuses with Democrats is not counted, and one elected as a Democratic candidate who later leaves remains counted.

Only the regular general election in each of the 435 congressional districts for the term beginning January 3, 2027 counts; a special election for a 119th Congress vacancy is disregarded whenever held. No district counts twice.

Seats are counted from Designated Media Source calls as they stand at the Expiration time, not from House composition on any later date; the eight rank equally. A seat is counted when at least four have declared its winner with no contradictory declaration then outstanding; withdrawn or superseded declarations are disregarded. A seat not counted under that four-of-eight test is attributed to the candidate the state certifies as elected. A runoff seat is counted when that contest is called.

Designated Media Source declarations. For United States based elections, this Contract may be resolved on an accelerated basis if (A) at least four (4) of the eight (8) Designated Media Sources have declared a winning candidate, party, or option, and (B) none of the Designated Media Sources have issued a contradictory declaration. “Designated Media Sources” are: The New York Times (NYT), The Associated Press (AP), Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ), CNN, Fox News, NBC News, CBS News, and ABC News. Should one of the Designated Media Sources cease to provide independent election calls, it may be replaced at the sole discretion of the Exchange. For the purposes of this clause, a source declares a winning candidate, party, or option when it makes either (i) a formal projection of victory by its centralized decision desk, or (ii) an unambiguous statement in a news article that the candidate/party/option has won. For the network sources (Fox, NBC, CBS, ABC), a declaration from a local affiliate may represent the parent network; however, a declaration from the national desk shall always supersede any affiliate’s call. In all instances, a parent network and all of its affiliates shall collectively constitute a single source for the purpose of this clause.

events.title: How many House seats will Democrats win in the Midterms?

markets.rules_primary: If the Democratic party has above 211 House seats on Feb 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Individuals caucusing with the Democrats will be included.

Clarification (11/12/26): Kalshi has filed an amendment to this market's Contract so that it can settle before February 1, 2027 once the election results have decided it. Starting November 26, 2026, Kalshi will check each party's seat count every day at 10:00 AM ET using Associated Press race calls, with a buffer for changes after the election (5 seats off the floor in the House, 1 in the Senate, and 1 seat added to the ceiling). Any market the results have decided will settle that morning; the rest will settle on February 1, 2027 as they do now. If the composition of Congress on February 1, 2027 would have paid an early-settled market the other way, Kalshi will credit $1.00 per contract for positions held on that side at 7:00 AM ET on November 12, 2026. Contracts bought after that time are not covered.

For example, as of November 11, 2026, the Associated Press has declared Democrats the winner of 254 House seats, with 13 seats undeclared. That gives Democrats a floor of 254 (seats declared) and a ceiling of 267 (254 plus the 13 undeclared), or 249 and 268 after the buffers. In KXDHOUSESEATS-27, every range from "Below 210" through "242-245" lies entirely below both values, so those markets would expire and settle No; "246-249" and "Above 249" each contain one of the two values, so they continue to trade and are checked again the next morning.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If the House Democratic Caucus adopts a rule limiting how long a member may serve as chair or ranking member of a House committee after Issuance and before Feb 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Only reporting from any of the Source Agencies qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

A term limit means a House Democratic Caucus rule that caps the number of terms or years a member may serve as chair or ranking member of a House committee. A cap that allows longer service with a waiver, or that exempts current chairs and ranking members, counts. A proposed or introduced amendment, a recommendation by a Caucus committee, a failed vote, and a limit on subcommittee leaders only do NOT count.

markets.rules_primary: If the number of California State Senate seats held by Democrats is at least 27 after the November 3, 2026 general election, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Each market counts the seats in that chamber held by the Democratic Party when the chamber's November 3, 2026 general election results are certified. Every seat on the 2026 ballot is attributed to its certified winner, and every other seat to the party designation the state election authority recorded for the winner of that seat's most recent general or special election, regardless of any vacancy, appointment or party change since that election. The number shown is that state's constitutional requirement to override a governor's veto, applied to the chamber's full membership, including where the state measures it against members present and voting. Vacancies, appointments and party changes after certification, and special elections held after November 3, 2026, are disregarded.

A winner counts as Democratic if the official results show the winner on the Democratic Party's ballot line or, where they show a combined designation, list Democratic first; a winner elected only on another party's line does not count.

markets.rules_secondary:
Re-establishing the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party counts, whether in the House rules resolution for the 120th Congress or in a separate resolution. A committee under a different name, or one that also covers other countries, counts if China or the Chinese Communist Party is expressly within its jurisdiction.

The following do NOT count:
An announcement or plan to establish the committee before the House adopts the resolution
Assigning China-related jurisdiction to a standing committee or subcommittee
A select committee on another subject, such as artificial intelligence, whose jurisdiction mentions China or the Chinese Communist Party only within that subject

Only reporting from the United States House of Representatives or any other Source Agency qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if any component becomes impossible to occur (resolving to No) or all components have been satisfied (resolving to Yes).
markets.no_sub_title: Will Democrats hold 218 or more seats in the House AND hold 49 or more seats in the Senate?
markets.rules_primary: If ALL of the following occur: Democrats hold 218 or more seats in the House after the 2026 midterms AND Democrats hold 49 or more seats in the Senate after the 2026 midterms, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This is a combination market requiring ALL specified outcomes to occur for the contract to pay out. If ANY single component resolves to No or becomes impossible, the entire contract immediately resolves to No. Each component is resolved according to its corresponding Kalshi ruleset: "Will Democrats hold 218 or more seats in the House?" uses SEATSCONGRESS, "Will Democrats hold 49 or more seats in the Senate?" uses SEATSCONGRESS. For economic data releases, resolution uses the first officially released value (not preliminary or revised estimates unless specified). All conditions must be satisfied within the specified time period.

This market will resolve based on the composition of the U.S. House of Representatives and the Senate on February 1, 2027. Individuals caucusing with either party will be included with them (e.g. an Independent who caucuses with a party, like Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders who caucuses with the Democrats, would be counted as a Democrat).

Clarification (11/12/26): Kalshi has filed an amendment that lets each seat-count leg of this combination event settle before February 1, 2027 once the election results have decided it. The combination settles Yes once every leg has settled Yes, or No as soon as any leg settles No. Starting November 26, 2026, each leg will be checked every day at 10:00 AM ET against Associated Press race calls, with a buffer for changes after the election (5 seats off the floor in the House, 1 in the Senate, and 1 seat added to the ceiling). If the composition of Congress on February 1, 2027 would have paid an early-settled market the other way, Kalshi will credit $1.00 per contract for positions held on that side at 7:00 AM ET on November 12, 2026. Contracts bought after that time are not covered.

For example, as of November 11, 2026, the Associated Press has declared Democrats the winner of 254 House seats, with 13 seats undeclared. That gives Democrats a floor of 254 (seats declared) and a ceiling of 267 (254 plus the 13 undeclared), or 249 and 268 after the buffers. In KXDHOUSESEATS-27, every range from "Below 210" through "242-245" lies entirely below both values, so those markets would expire and settle No; "246-249" and "Above 249" each contain one of the two values, so they continue to trade and are checked again the next morning.

This is a combination market requiring ALL specified outcomes to occur for the contract to pay out. If ANY single component resolves to No or becomes impossible, the entire contract immediately resolves to No. Each component is resolved according to its corresponding Kalshi ruleset: "Will Democrats hold 235 or more seats in the House?" uses SEATSCONGRESS, "Will Democrats hold 51 or more seats in the Senate?" uses SEATSCONGRESS. For economic data releases, resolution uses the first officially released value (not preliminary or revised estimates unless specified). All conditions must be satisfied within the specified time period.

This market will resolve based on the composition of the U.S. House of Representatives and the Senate on February 1, 2027. Individuals caucusing with either party will be included with them (e.g. an Independent who caucuses with a party, like Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders who caucuses with the Democrats, would be counted as a Democrat).

Clarification (11/12/26): Kalshi has filed an amendment that lets each seat-count leg of this combination event settle before February 1, 2027 once the election results have decided it. The combination settles Yes once every leg has settled Yes, or No as soon as any leg settles No. Starting November 26, 2026, each leg will be checked every day at 10:00 AM ET against Associated Press race calls, with a buffer for changes after the election (5 seats off the floor in the House, 1 in the Senate, and 1 seat added to the ceiling). If the composition of Congress on February 1, 2027 would have paid an early-settled market the other way, Kalshi will credit $1.00 per contract for positions held on that side at 7:00 AM ET on November 12, 2026. Contracts bought after that time are not covered.

For example, as of November 11, 2026, the Associated Press has declared Democrats the winner of 254 House seats, with 13 seats undeclared. That gives Democrats a floor of 254 (seats declared) and a ceiling of 267 (254 plus the 13 undeclared), or 249 and 268 after the buffers. In KXDHOUSESEATS-27, every range from "Below 210" through "242-245" lies entirely below both values, so those markets would expire and settle No; "246-249" and "Above 249" each contain one of the two values, so they continue to trade and are checked again the next morning.

If the case is dismissed for lack of jurisdiction, that counts as a ruling only if the judgment refers to jurisdiction
Sua sponte rulings count if they match the specified judgment
Per curiam opinions and summary orders count as rulings
If multiple judges issue separate opinions, the majority/plurality opinion controls

markets.rules_primary: If the Alternative fuer Deutschland has entered a German state government after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Only reporting from any of the Source Agencies qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

The Alternative fuer Deutschland is part of a German state government only if one or more of its representatives hold at least one ministerial or cabinet-level position, including a junior ministerial or equivalent executive role, in that state's government.

The test applies at any time after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027, whether the position is taken at the formation of a new state government or through a mid-term appointment or reshuffle
A caretaker or acting administration carried over from a previous government does NOT count
An arrangement in which the party supports a minority government without holding any such position does NOT count
A coalition agreement that has been signed but under which no government has yet taken office does NOT count

Report dates determine inclusion in the period regardless of publication time, subject to the contract's Expiration rules; days without a qualifying report are disregarded.

Use each report date's initial non-preliminary value. A correction, retraction or removal before Expiration supersedes it only if the Exchange determines it remedies a material error. If no reliable qualifying data is available by Expiration, markets resolve to the last fair price determined by the Exchange under the certified no-data provisions.

The latest expiration and last trading time are February 7, 2027, 10:00 AM EST, one week after the final observation day. A strike that satisfies the payout criterion may close and expire earlier in accordance with Rule 7.2. The observation cutoff does not change when expiration is later.

markets.rules_primary: If Tesla robotaxi service is offered to the general public in Arizona before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For "offered to": Tesla has launched a robotaxi service in Arizona that satisfies ALL of the following criteria:

The service allows members of the general public to request rides through a publicly accessible application or platform (not limited to Tesla employees, beta testers, or invite-only participants)
The vehicles operate without any human driver or safety monitor physically present in the driver's seat who is actively controlling the vehicle during normal operation
The service charges fares or fees for rides (free promotional rides alone do not qualify)

For "removed from": Tesla has discontinued, suspended, or withdrawn a previously operational robotaxi service in Arizona that met all the "offered to" criteria above, where:

The service is no longer accepting new ride requests from the general public for any period of time as a result of a decision by Tesla to suspend operations in the area, and such suspension is not explicitly characterized as temporary (e.g., due to weather, maintenance, or system upgrades). The Payout Criterion is not satisfied by short-term service interruptions that are clearly communicated as temporary or expected to resume.

The following do NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion:

If a government orders Tesla to cease ongoing services but they do not comply, then the market does not resolve to Yes
Services limited to Tesla employees, contractors, or their guests
Beta tests, pilot programs, or demonstrations
Services requiring special invitations, access codes, or pre-approval to use
Vehicles with human safety drivers, monitors, or operators in any seat of the vehicle who can take control
Temporary suspensions due to weather or technical issues
Services operating only with remote human teleoperators controlling each vehicle continuously
Test fleets that are not charging fares to the general public
Announcements of future launches without actual operational service

markets.rules_primary: If BJP wins the most wards in the next Kolkata Municipal Corporation election, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The winner is the party winning the most wards in the next general election to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (not a by-election to a single ward).
Each ward elects one councillor. A ward counts for the party on whose symbol its winning candidate contested.
Allied parties are counted separately, and wards won by independents, including party-backed independents, count for no party.
Mamata Trinamool and Ritabrata Trinamool are the Trinamool Congress factions led by Mamata Banerjee and Ritabrata Banerjee, each counted separately under whatever name and symbol it contests with.
If two parties win the same number of wards, the one with the higher share of the vote across all wards resolves Yes and all others No.

This market is eligible for accelerated resolution by a consensus of media calls. See full rules for details.

Alphabetical order by surname - If both criteria above are still tied, players are ordered alphabetically by their family name

The difference between the two margins is rounded to two decimal places, and a range includes its lower number but not its upper number.

Resolution will use the final 2026 calendar-year total reported by Boise Airport, including the December 2026 statistics/YTD figure. Boise Airport states that monthly statistics are typically released approximately 30 days after the end of each month.

markets.rules_primary: If the U.S. dollar’s share of international payments by value on Swift, excluding payments within the Eurozone, for December 2026 is above 57.0%, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The Underlying is the percentage share attributed to USD for December 2026 in the “International payments currency - Excluding payments within Eurozone” table published by Swift in its Global Currency Tracker. The statistic is based on the value of live and delivered MT 103, MT 202, and equivalent ISO 20022 payment messages exchanged on Swift, including customer-initiated and institutional payments.

This market will use the first value published by Swift for December 2026. Corrections or revisions published after Expiration will not be considered.

If Swift changes the title, format, or location of the Global Currency Tracker but continues to publish a materially equivalent statistic, the corresponding successor publication may be used.

markets.rules_primary: If the Pyth security yield for the 5-Year U.S. Treasury Note is above 4.38% at Jan 28, 2027 at 8:45am ET, the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Settlement uses the closing Pyth yield of the one-minute candlestick immediately preceding the settlement time. For an 8:45am ET observation, use the 8:44am candle, covering 8:44:00am up to but excluding 8:45:00am ET. No averaging applies. The closing Pyth yield, expressed as a percentage, is rounded to five decimal places using round-half-up before comparison with the strike.

Other sources and stale or carried-forward values cannot substitute. If reliable data is unavailable by expiration, or none is expected, settlement is at the Exchange-determined last fair price, unless a "No data" strike is listed. Corrections, expiration and Rule 7.1 review follow the full contract rules. Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the Pyth Data Association. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

The economic event named in the title provides context. The published observation date and time govern; a delayed or rescheduled economic release does not automatically change that observation time.
